about: Toolsmith's run table (03 3.3 run note 2): one row per kind of project, first match wins. 'when' names a test in runbook._WHEN; commands use {P} (the assigned port), {pm} (the package runner), {dir} (the built folder), {expose} (a Dockerfile's port), {name} (its image), {script}, {readme_cmd}. 'via': start_server (a server BuildBot keeps) or run (it ends). Every command is one program and its arguments: no shell (D60). Harvested from bb-next@63c8a037:src/puffpai/build/runbook.py RUN_TABLE.

rows.why: its own compose file (BuildBot runs a local copy on 127.0.0.1)

rows.stack: client-only app, built then served as static files
rows.why: build once, then serve the built folder; no long-running dev server

rows.fallback: {pm} run build; then npx next start -p {P} -H 127.0.0.1

rows.start: npm start (the Core gives it PORT and HOST)

rows.build: write_file compose.yaml with one service: build: . and ports: ["127.0.0.1:{P}:{expose}"] (a try runs Docker only as docker compose)

rows.stack: Node app with its own start script
rows.start: {pm} run {script} (the Core gives it PORT and HOST)
rows.why: its package.json says how it starts (a server of its own), not static files

rows.install: python -m venv .venv, then its requirements into .venv
